front.title: Signed Reasoning Traces of CIRIS Agents

abstract.t:
An AI agent that acts on a person's behalf reaches each action through a sequence of steps: it gathers context, runs several evaluations, selects an action, submits the selection to checks that can veto it, and then acts. Most of those steps are calls to language models.
This document specifies the CIRIS reasoning trace: one signed record per unit of agent work (a thought), sealed when the action is taken. The trace lists every step and every model call in the order the recording component received them, with scores, outcomes, sizes, costs and durations, and, at higher disclosure levels, reasoning text and the prompts and completions themselves. It specifies three disclosure levels, the exact bytes the agent's Ed25519 signature covers, how a trace is carried as a row of the CIRIS Epistemic Grammar (CEG), when a trace exists at all, and the checks a consumer runs before relying on one. It records where the published specification and the shipping implementation disagree.
